finding.claim: HIGH: The /preview endpoint fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no allowlist, scheme restriction or IP filtering, and returns the status code and the first 500 characters of the body. An unauthenticated caller can reach internal services, loopback and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. requests follows redirects by default, so a redirect from an external host would reach internal targets as well. Redirect risk: yes. Reproduction: curl 'http://HOST/preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/'. Fix: parse the URL, compare .hostname against a strict allowlist, and set allow_redirects=False. Optionally resolve the host and block RFC-1918, loopback and link-local ranges.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:15 (query parameter 'url' of GET /preview)
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, with the response returned via jsonify at app.py:17

trace.note: @app.route('/preview') is a public Flask route with no authentication decorator
target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-controlled value
requests.get(target, timeout=5) is called with the value unchanged and redirects followed by default
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF rather than blind

finding.guards_checked: No validation exists between source and sink: no hostname allowlist, no scheme check, no IP or CIDR filtering, no allow_redirects=False. There is no auth on the route, and no egress controls are present in the repo. Considered and rejected as mitigations: the 5s timeout and the 500-character truncation, neither of which blocks access to internal or metadata endpoints.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the unauthenticated query param `url` and passes it unchanged to requests.get at app.py:16, with status and body[:500] returned at app.py:17. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check exists only in /partner (app.py:23-25), not in /preview.
